newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 20.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 20.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:

** Foreign investors registered on Indian stock exchanges invested $55 million in the two weeks to January 15 according to latest data available from market-regulator the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the Business Standard newspaper said on Monday.
The newspaper said inflows by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) -- which hit $12.2 million in the first ten days of January -- jumped sharply last week.
** The Economic Times says the final draft of the new takeover guidelines has been submitted to the stock market regulator by the draft committee.

Equality of treatment to all shareholders, protection of shareholder interests and fair and truthful disclosure of all material information by acquirers form part of the guiding principles of the draft, the paper says.

** The Bombay Stock Exchange has informed Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda that market capitalisation in the exchange has recovered by 720 billion rupees since early December due to statements made by the Prime Minister and promise of a package to infuse life into the capital markets, the Business Standard reports.
The BSE president, M G Damani was quoted as saying the 30-share BSE index would touch the 4,500 mark by December if the forthcoming Union Budget is favourable.

** Automobiles Peugeot, the French partner in PAL-Peugeot is keen on raising stake in the Indian joint venture to 48 percent from 32 percent despite reported resistance to the move by PAL, the Economic Times reports.

The paper quoted an official of the French company as saying Peugeot is shortly going to make an application with the Foreign Investment Promotion Board and other statutory bodies for permission to raise the stake.

** The Indian rupee opened at 35.850/860 against the dollar on Monday compared to Friday's close of 35.84/85, dealers said. The rupee is seen staying in a tight range, over-supply of dollars seen colouring the sentiment.
** India's overheated stock markets seen likely to cool this week with market players unwinding positions after a steep rise in interest costs, dealers and analysts said at the weekend.
Carry-forward rates leapt to an annualised 40-45 percent on Saturday at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) against 15-17 percent a week ago.

The BSE's benchmark 30-share index closed last week with a minor gain of 4.03 points at 3,422.35 after a roller-coaster ride that saw the index hitting a five- month high of 3,812.31 during an early rally on Thursday.
